board.name: Tennessee Board of Physician Assistants (formerly the Committee on Physician Assistants of the Board of Medical Examiners)

licence.title: Physician Assistant licence
licence.renewalDeadline: Last day of the licensee's birth month, biennial birthdate renewal system (Rule 1130-01-.09(1)(a))

ce.categoryRules: 100 hours in the 2 years before renewal; at least 50 must be Category I; programs approved by the AMA, AAPA or NCCPA. Proof period follows the NCCPA 2 year cycle for certified PAs, or a birth year based equivalent for non certified PAs.

topicMandates.topic: Controlled substance prescribing including TN Department of Health treatment guidelines on opioids, benzodiazepines, barbiturates and carisoprodol (Category I)
Opioid addiction risks course(s) approved by the board, after notice that the PA was identified as a high risk prescriber (T.C.A. 68-1-128)
topicMandates.appliesTo: PAs identified by the Department of Health as high risk prescribers

ce.controlledSubstanceCe: 2 Category I hours every cycle for all PAs (Rule 1130-01-.12(1)(a)). PAs identified as high risk prescribers must complete approved course(s) totalling at least 20 hours on opioid addiction risks (Board of Physician Assistants policy approved July 18, 2025).

practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Written protocol jointly developed and signed by PA and supervising physician, kept at the practice location and reviewed at least every 2 years; notify the board of the primary supervising physician and of any change within 15 days.
practice.notes: Public Chapter 1042 (2024) renames the relationship 'collaborating physician' and creates board 'endorsement' (6,000 postgraduate clinical hours) allowing practice under a collaborative agreement instead of protocols, but the act's operative effective date is the effective date of task force rules not yet in force; April 2026 board minutes target January 2027. The published rule chapter 1130-01 is still the August 2021 revision.

prescribing.separateAuthorityRegistration: Notice of Authorization for Prescribing form (with formulary) filed with the board and the Tennessee Board of Pharmacy before prescribing (Rule 1130-01-.21(2)).
prescribing.ceForPrescribers: 2 Category I hours in controlled substance prescribing every cycle (applies to all PAs).

rn.ceNote: No fixed hour count: RNs attest to a personal competence file with at least 2 items from a 14 item menu each renewal period (Rule 1000-01-.18(2)); one option is 10 contact hours of CE, another is current national certification.

aprn.title: APRN certificate (role: Nurse Practitioner); prescribing requires a Certificate of Fitness
aprn.separateLicenceOrCertificate: certificate (APRN certificate plus Certificate of Fitness to prescribe)

topicMandates.topic: Controlled substance prescribing including TN Department of Health treatment guidelines on opioids, benzodiazepines, barbiturates and carisoprodol
topicMandates.appliesTo: APRNs holding a Certificate of Fitness

aprn.note: Renewal competence for APRNs = evidence of national certification plus 1 item from the RN competence list; Certificate of Fitness holders add 2 contact hours of controlled substance prescribing CE. Initial Certificate of Fitness requires 3 quarter hours of pharmacology instruction (education, not recurring CE).

prescribing.separateAuthorityRegistration: Certificate of Fitness from the Board of Nursing, plus a notice filed with the board before prescribing (formulary and collaborating physician name), updated before any change.
prescribing.controlledSubstanceCe: 2 contact hours every renewal period (Certificate of Fitness holders)

practice.agreementType: collaboration (protocols with a collaborating physician; BME Rule 0880-06 uses 'supervising physician')
practice.agreementFilingAndRenewal: Prescribing APRN must have a collaborating physician complying with BME Rule 0880-06: protocols required, jointly developed, dated and signed, reviewed and updated biennially, kept at the practice site; the physician reviews at least 20% of charts every 30 days, personally reviews and signs within 30 days any chart where a controlled drug was prescribed or a prescription fell outside the protocols, and visits any remote site at least every 30 days. Notice to the Board of Nursing names the collaborating physician and formulary and must be updated before prescribing under any change.
practice.authorityNote: 'restricted' is the AANP classification label; the primary rules confirm a collaborating physician is required for prescribing.

unverified: PA and NP: Tennessee CSMD registration for prescribers with a DEA registration (T.C.A. 53-10-305) was not confirmed: the statute is only on Lexis and Justia returned 403, and CSMD Rule 1140-11 does not state the registration duty. stateCsRegistrationRequired stays null; Tennessee has no separate state controlled substance licence in any source loaded.

PA: whether current NCCPA certification is accepted in lieu of the 100 hour requirement is not stated in Rule 1130-01-.12; left null. The board page ties the Category I/II split to NCCPA while the rule sets at least 50 Category I.

PA: Public Chapter 1042 (2024) endorsement and collaborative agreement framework is enacted but not operative until task force rules take effect (April 17, 2026 minutes target January 2027). On 2026-10-01 the SOS index still lists only 1130-01.20210816. Recheck before shipping.

NP: 'restricted' practice authority is the AANP classification label, not a term in Tennessee law; the collaborating physician requirement is confirmed in Rule 1000-04-.04(6) and BME Rule 0880-06 (August 2004 revision, still says 'supervising physician').
